Three of these use cases are explored in the following sections. Figure 6: Use Case Model Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory 17 LLNL-TR-2004679 Sequence diagrams The Prepare to Survey use case is illustrated via the sequence diagram in Figure 7. This use case is critical because it allows the Operator to configure all necessary aspects of the survey such as boundary, survey type, and use of chemicals. The Operator first provides their credentials, which are verified by SCCOUT. From there, the Operator selects the survey type (agricultural, range, etc.), target, and boundaries. SCCOUT filters the information through a database and recommends appropriate pesticides and herbicides if necessary. When the tank has reached an appropriate fill level, SCCOUT will send a final request confirmation to the Operator and waits for an acknowledgement before beginning work. Figure 7: Setup Survey Sequence Diagram Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory 18 LLNL-TR-2004679 The Request Maintenance use case is illustrated via the sequence diagram in Figure 8. SCCOUT recognizes failure and sends a report to the Operator. The Operator sends a maintenance request to SCCOUT which triggers a request to the Mechanics. A solution plan is created by Mechanics, which is relayed to the Operator through SCCOUT. The Operator approves the plan, and SCCOUT forwards that approval to the Mechanics. At this point the Mechanics conduct maintenance and compile a report of the services performed. The Mechanics submit the report to SCCOUT, which forwards a copy to the Operator. The Operator is then given the opportunity to inspect the repaired equipment and submits approval to SCCOUT that the performed services are satisfactory. Figure 8: Request Maintenance Sequence Diagram Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory 19 LLNL-TR-2004679 The Responding to Distress Response use case is illustrated via the sequence diagram in Figure 9. SCCOUT first recognizes one of several registered issues and sends error codes to the Operator, Software Developers, and Mechanics. Additionally, the Operator receives SCCOUT’s GPS location. SCCOUT sends the Software Developers and Mechanics an inquiry for the software support or physical maintenance relevance of the issue. They respond accordingly with the issue’s relevance to their scope of work and a basic plan of action. SCCOUT forwards these reports and a request for assistance (following the suggested plan of action) to the Operator. The Operator can then proceed to follow the recommended plan of action in resolving the issue. Figure 9: Respond to Distress Response Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory 20 LLNL-TR-2004679 10.
